chunks: Ali (peace be upon him) raised it (in the chain of narration), he said:

Abu Hanifa asked Abu Ja'far Muhammad (peace be upon him), so he said to him: 'O Abu Ja'far! What do you say regarding Mut'a (temporary marriage)? Do you claim that it is halal (permissible)?' He said: 'Yes.'
He said: 'So what prevents you from instructing your womenfolk that they should be enjoyed (perform Mut'a) and earn for you?'
So Abu Ja'far said to him: 'Not every craft/work is desired in it, even though it may be permissible, and people have different capacities and ranks which elevate their capacities.'
'But what do you say, O Abu Hanifa, regarding Al-Nabeez (a type of drink)? Do you claim that it is permissible?' So he said: 'Yes.'
He said: 'So what prevents you from getting your womenfolk to sit in the shops as sellers of Nabeez, so they would earn for you?'
So Abu Hanifa said: 'One with one, and your share is more effective (or: your share is purer/stronger).'

Then he said to him: 'O Abu Ja'far! The Verse in the chapter 'Sa'ala Sa'il' speaks with the prohibition of Mut'a, and the narration from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) has come with its abrogation.'
So Abu Ja'far said to him: 'O Abu Hanifa! The Chapter 'Sa'ala Sa'il' is Meccan, and the Verse of Mut'a is Medinite, and your narration is abnormal (shadh) and refuted.'
So Abu Hanifa said to him: 'And the Verse of Inheritance also speaks with the abrogation of Mut'a.'
So Abu Ja'far said: 'Marriage is established without inheritance.'
Abu Hanifa said: 'From where do you say that?'
So Abu Ja'far said: 'If a man from the Muslims were to marry a woman from the People of the Book, then he dies from her, what would you say regarding it?'
He said: 'She does not inherit from him.'
He said: 'So marriage is established without inheritance.' Then they departed.

key_terms.سُورَةُ سَأَلَ سَائِل: Surat Sa'ala Sa'il (Chapter Al-Haqqah, Surah 69 or Al-Ma'arij, Surah 70 depending on context, here referring to the verse of abrogation)

ai.seo_question: What is the argument between Abu Hanifa and Imam al-Baqir regarding Mut'a and abrogation?
ai.summary: This dialogue, recorded in *Al-Kafi*, highlights the jurisprudential dispute between the emerging Hanafi school and the Ahl al-Bayt regarding the validity of *Mut'a* (temporary marriage). Imam al-Baqir employs logical analogies (*qiyas*) to expose inconsistencies in Abu Hanifa’s reasoning, specifically refuting the claim of abrogation (*naskh*) by distinguishing between the Meccan and Medinan periods of revelation. The narrative underscores the Shia emphasis on the continuity of marriage and inheritance rights, even in cases where specific legal conditions, such as inheritance from a spouse of the People of the Book, do not apply.
